summary: GLP-1-only radar for 2026-09-28. The EASD 2026 meeting opens today in Milan (Sep 28–Oct 2), so expect a week of new abstracts, which favours topics that are emerging now. Verified top picks: (1) stopping GLP-1s and losing the heart benefit (BMJ Medicine, 333k veterans), already moving through local TV syndication; (2) tirzepatide switching on brown fat, framed carefully because it is a mouse-only study; (3) orforglipron working about equally well before, during and after menopause (EASD post-hoc analysis); (4) the EASD cohort suggesting people with BMI 25–27 and inflammation have heart risk similar to people who already qualify (observational only). Next come the carry-over SELECT mediation story (seen 5 times, holding around 72), hair loss (Guardian coverage plus a new Clinical Dermatology review), cannabis with GLP-1s and stomach problems, the NAION lawsuits (peaking; our angle is absolute risk), and GLP-1 vs CPAP for sleep apnea. Pipeline items (CagriSema vs tirzepatide, Viking's monthly maintenance shot) are a step behind. We reject microdosing and 'research peptide' retatrutide because they break our guardrails. Several items carry a 'caution' rating: they need strict hedging (mouse data, FAERS signals, observational designs), and any story about stopping must avoid advice to stop or change medication.

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1s may erase the heart benefit: after 2 years off, risk of heart attack, stroke and death up to 22% higher (BMJ Medicine, 333,000+ US veterans with type 2 diabetes)
candidates.angle: 'Why GLP-1 is treated like a long-term medicine, just as blood pressure pills are.' Explain what came back after stopping (inflammation, blood pressure, cholesterol, not just weight) and list the questions to bring to your prescriber before any change. Don't give stop/start advice. It's observational, so say 'linked to', and note this was a type 2 diabetes population.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: The WashU press release was syndicated to many Scripps local stations on Sep 27, with Axios and ScienceDaily coverage too. 'Should I stop?' is one of the biggest questions in our audience, and creator explainers with the real numbers are still thin.

evidence.signal: 333k veterans, 3-year follow-up; risk rises with longer gaps, up to 22% after 2 years off
Science press pickup
Mainstream local-TV syndication Sep 27

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) switched on calorie-burning brown fat, beyond eating less (obese mice, Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does tirzepatide make you burn more, not just eat less?' Walk through what brown fat is and what 'batokines' are, then be upfront that this is a mouse result. Contrast it with what the human SURMOUNT trials actually showed. The hook is curiosity; the honest payoff is 'promising, not proven in people'.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily ran it Sep 26, followed by Men's Journal, AOL, Health and Me and SSBCrack on Sep 27. It's spreading into lifestyle media while YouTube coverage is still minimal.

evidence.signal: Mouse study; the effect persisted after controlling for food intake; authors warn it may not apply to humans
Lifestyle media pickup Sep 27

candidates.topic: The daily GLP-1 pill orforglipron gave similar weight loss before, during and after menopause (ATTAIN-1/ATTAIN-2 post-hoc analysis, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause blunt GLP-1 weight loss? New data says maybe not.' Women in all three stages lost up to about 14% of body weight, and up to 83% lost at least 5% (vs 30% on placebo). Tie it to muscle and bone priorities after menopause. It's a post-hoc analysis with 142–225 women per group.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD, which opens today. Medscape and Medical Xpress covered it Sep 26. Our audience is heavily women 40–65, and menopause stories have been our strongest recurring snapshots.

evidence.signal: Up to 14% weight loss across stages; 142–225 women per arm; post-hoc
Clinician press pickup

candidates.topic: Overweight but not 'eligible'? People with BMI 25–27 plus inflammation or high remnant cholesterol had 41–47% higher coronary risk (EASD 2026, 313,145 UK Biobank + Copenhagen adults)
candidates.angle: 'BMI isn't the whole story for heart risk.' Explain remnant cholesterol and hs-CRP as questions to raise at a checkup, and explain why this is not evidence that GLP-1s help this group yet. The authors say trials are needed. Link it to SELECT's actual population.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress published it Sep 27, timed for EASD, which opens today. The 'who should get GLP-1s' debate is heating up.

evidence.signal: 313,145 adults, observational, conference abstract not yet peer-reviewed; authors say trials needed

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only about 20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation analysis, European Heart Journal), plus who lost the most weight in SELECT (Diabetes Care)
candidates.angle: 'Your scale isn't the only thing your heart cares about.' Explain what the other ~80% might be (inflammation, blood pressure, direct vessel effects, framed as hypotheses) and add the Diabetes Care predictors of peak weight loss. Population: adults with heart disease and overweight/obesity, without diabetes.

why does ozempic protect the heart

candidates.angle: 'Two things that slow your stomach.' Explain gastric emptying simply, why it matters before surgery and anesthesia, and what to tell your care team. Stay neutral and non-judgmental. Evidence is mostly mechanism plus observational data, so hedge.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 'eye stroke' (NAION) lawsuits: what the actual risk is (EMA: very rare, about 1 extra case per 10,000 person-years in type 2 diabetes studies)
candidates.angle: 'Headlines vs numbers.' Put the absolute risk in context and note the EU label vs US label difference. Explain which sudden vision symptoms need urgent care, without fear-mongering or suggesting anyone stop their medicine.
candidates.why_now: The MDL has 216 cases and expert hearings ran Sep 10–18. NewsNation, AOL, MassLive and Fox are covering it. Our differentiator is calm, absolute-risk framing.

evidence.signal: 216 cases in MDL-3163 as of Sep 1, 2026

candidates.topic: GLP-1s cut sleep apnea events by about 6–22 per hour, but CPAP (about 31/hour) is still the top treatment (JAMA Otolaryngology review)
candidates.angle: 'Better together, not either/or.' Explain AHI simply and note that tirzepatide is FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe OSA with obesity. Explain why anatomy matters, and why you shouldn't ditch CPAP without your sleep doctor.
